wi_1_hawk_s_nest.blurb: Hawk's Nest is a quiet, out-of-the-way cliff on the western end of the East Rampart above Devil's Lake, in the Baraboo Range near Baraboo. It holds some of the longest lines on that band, all on quartzite and all protected with your own gear, as the lake has no bolted routes. Most of the 26 climbs are trad leads, with a handful of top-rope lines and one boulder problem. Grades run from easy fifth-class up to the low 5.12s, with a good cluster in the 5.7 range and another at 5.11. Reaching the base takes a trail walk along the rim and a gully descent, so expect a longer day than at the busier buttresses to the east.

wi_02_many_pines_buttress.blurb: Many Pines Buttress is a steep, tall quartzite face roughly a third of the way along the East Rampart at Devil's Lake State Park, outside Baraboo in the Baraboo Range. It is a trad crag: nearly all of the 25 climbs are gear leads, with a few top-rope options and a single boulder problem. The spread is wide, from 5.3 beginner terrain through the middle grades to a strong set of 5.11 and 5.12 lines, so it suits both newer leaders and strong ones. Reaching it means a climb up the CCC trail and a short walk along the climbers' path under the cliff. Expect long sustained pitches and a good deal of company on weekends.

wi_08_two_pines_buttress.blurb: Two Pines Buttress sits on the East Rampart of Devil's Lake State Park near Baraboo, Wisconsin, just beside Many Pines Buttress. This quartzite wall has 24 climbs, nearly all trad with three top-rope lines. Moderate routes dominate, with many at 5.7 and a few easier ones, and then a step up to a tougher group between 5.10 and 5.12 for stronger parties. The eastern half has long, unbroken lines, while the western side is split by a ledge. There are no bolts at the lake, so bring a full rack. The walk up the CCC trail takes a good chunk of time, but the base is easy to find.

wi_parthenon_the.blurb: The Parthenon is a bouldering zone on the north side of Hagar Mountain, in the forests of northern Wisconsin near the village of Mountain. It is the busiest and most developed part of the mountain, with 25 problems that are mostly tall highballs. Difficulty covers a huge range, from V1 up to V10, with plenty of V3 to V5 lines in the middle and a handful of very hard ones at the top. It feels remote, with a long forest walk and a scramble down ramps to get in, so bring pads, a spotter or two and good judgment. Not a place for a casual first outing.

wi_wisconsin_strip.blurb: The Wisconsin Strip is the northernmost cliff on the Wisconsin bank of the St. Croix River, in Interstate Park at St. Croix Falls. It offers a dense line-up of routes that are long for the Midwest, on basalt, split between gear leads and top-rope climbs. With 24 routes, most grades sit between easy fifth-class and 5.13, with a bunch in the 5.9 to 5.10 range and some hard lines at the top end. The cliff is popular with both climbers and passing hikers, so it is often busy. Getting to the base takes a third-class gully on the cliff's northern side.

wi_amazing_pillar.blurb: Amazing Pillar is a short band of quartzite along the south rim at Devil's Lake State Park, beside the Reserve bouldering zone above Baraboo. It has 24 boulder problems with a lopsided spread: a big pack of easy V1s, a thin middle, and a few hard problems up to about V9. The namesake line is regarded as one of the best V6s in the park. Faces point in several directions, including west and south. It sits a good uphill hike from the lake, so it tends to be quieter than the lakeside boulders, but it is worth the effort for the quality lines.

wi_barrel_ridge_proper.blurb: Barrel Ridge Proper is the main bouldering ridge in Twin Valley, within Governor Dodge State Park in southwest Wisconsin. This sandstone ridge holds 24 problems, most about 15 feet tall, with generally flat landings. Difficulty is friendly: mostly V0 to V4, with a couple of lines reaching V5 or V6. Walls are close to vertical, and the taller, cleaner faces are on the south end. It is a small area, but the stone is among the best in the park, and the walk in is short. Bring a pad and a spotter for the taller problems.
wi_barrel_ridge_proper.approach: Climb the steep hillside and loop around a small bluff to a trail, then follow it along past a short sandstone pillar to the start of the ridge.
